title: A Step Harder, Not a Step Too Far: The Benefits and Limits of Curriculum Difficulty Progression in GRPO
abstract: arXiv:2610.13669v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Curriculum learning typically organizes training samples from easy to hard. In GRPO, medium-difficulty samples are attractive for online selection because they are more likely to yield informative group-relative learning signals, and prioritizing them can improve training efficiency. However, it remains unclear whether persistently selecting such samples also leads to the strongest final model performance, or whether training can benefit from progressing toward harder samples. Meanwhile, sample difficulty changes as the policy evolves, so fixed difficulty estimates can become misaligned with the current policy. translated_title: 更进一步而非过犹不及：GRPO中课程难度递进的收益与局限
translated_abstract: 课程学习通常按照从易到难的顺序组织训练样本。在GRPO中，中等难度的样本对在线选择颇具吸引力，因为它们更有可能产生信息丰富的组间相对学习信号，优先选择这些样本可以提升训练效率。然而，持续选择此类样本是否也能带来最强的最终模型性能，或者训练是否能从向更难样本推进中获益，目前仍不清楚。同时，样本难度会随策略的演化而变化，固定的难度估计可能与当前策略产生偏差。为此，我们在当前策略下重新估计样本难度，并受课程学习从易到难原则的启发，设计并评估了一种分阶段课程，将活跃难度区间逐步向更难的样本推进。在GSM8K上的实验表明，持续选择中等难度样本并不能（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出在GRPO训练中基于当前策略动态重估样本难度，并设计逐步向更难样本推进的分阶段课程，实验表明持续只选中等难度样本并非最优，适度渐进地提升难度才能带来更强的最终性能，但难度提升也存在限度。
en_tdlr: The paper proposes dynamically re-estimating sample difficulty under the current policy in GRPO with a staged easy-to-hard curriculum, showing that persistently selecting medium-difficulty samples is suboptimal, and that gradually progressing toward harder samples improves final performance—though only up to a limit.
